name: FL-24
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+22 partisan lean gives Democrats a decisive structural edge in this open Miami-area seat
Gilbert has raised roughly four times as much as Brown ($1.3M vs. $313K)
Over $2M in outside spending opposing Gilbert, triple the support on his side, signals GOP investment
No public polls; Polymarket prices a Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: The district's D+22 lean and Gilbert's clear fundraising advantage make a Democratic hold the strong expectation even with Frederica Wilson retiring. Heavy outside spending against Gilbert keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated, but it is unlikely to close a twenty-point structural gap.
model.watch: Escalating outside spending against Gilbert or an unusually strong Republican turnout edge in Miami-Dade could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Frederica Wilson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Democrats are strong favorites to hold this open Miami-area seat after Frederica Wilson's retirement. The district's D+22 partisan lean gives any Democratic nominee a large head start, and the underlying fundamentals point the same direction. Polymarket prices a Democratic win at roughly 96 percent, and the seat is not considered contested by serious observers.

Oliver Gilbert has raised about four times as much as Republican Te Mayonna Brown, though outside groups have spent heavily against him—more than $2 million, about three times what has backed his campaign. That spending shows Republican interest but would need to overcome a decades-long Democratic margin to matter. With no public polling available, uncertainty rests mainly on turnout in a nationally favorable environment for Republicans. Even so, the seat's structural lean makes an upset a long shot.
